title: cPanel Flaw Lets Attackers Take Full Server Control With Root Access
content_md: A newly disclosed vulnerability in cPanel and WHM , the widely deployed web hosting management platform, could allow a low-privilege authenticated user to obtain root-level control of an entire server. Tracked as CVE-2026-65643, the issue affects cPanel’s domain parking functionality and was publicly detailed in a security advisory published on August 27, 2026, by cPanel support engineer Devon Courtney. The vulnerability is particularly serious for shared-hosting and reseller environments, where numerous unrelated customers may operate on the same physical or virtual server. cPanel Flaw Lets Attackers Take Full Server Control According to cPanel, an authenticated account with permission to add parked or addon domains can exploit the flaw to create arbitrary files on the underlying server. That capability can ultimately result in code execution with root privileges, allowing an attacker to bypass the normal isolation boundaries separating hosting accounts. Domain parking is a standard cPanel feature that enables customers to direct additional domain names to an existing website without creating a separate hosting account. Because parked and addon domains are commonly enabled across shared-hosting environments, the affected functionality could be broadly accessible to ordinary customer accounts.
